drugs.name: Dapsone
drugs.mechanism: PABA analog that inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; bacteriostatic. Resistance: altered dihydropteroate synthase, decreased uptake or increased PABA production
drugs.adverseEffects: Acts like a sulfonamide: hemolysis with bite cells in G6PD deficiency, kernicterus in a neonate, rash up to Stevens-Johnson, crystalluria, interstitial nephritis; cross-allergy with sulfa drugs
drugs.use: Hansen disease (leprosy); Pneumocystis prophylaxis in HIV; topical form for severe acne

drugs.name: Clofazimine
drugs.mechanism: Lipophilic drug with long bactericidal action; binds guanine in mycobacterial DNA and suppresses T lymphocytes (anti-inflammatory); raises reactive oxygen species
drugs.adverseEffects: Pinkish discoloration of skin and conjunctiva; GI upset including GI bleeding; QT prolongation; rare splenic rupture; not used in pregnancy
drugs.use: Hansen disease; not stocked by pharmacies - the physician registers as an investigator with the National Hansen's Disease Program, which supplies it

drugs.name: Thalidomide
drugs.mechanism: Lowers TNF-alpha and decreases angiogenesis; a racemic drug whose (S) enantiomer is the teratogen
drugs.adverseEffects: Short or absent limb long bones (phocomelia) after first-trimester exposure; requires pregnancy tests at the start and during therapy and two forms of birth control
drugs.use: Erythema nodosum leprosum, the severe inflammatory reaction of leprosy; multiple myeloma
